correctness.rationale: The full graph and ordinary outsider signature predicate are specified exactly. Monotonicity reduces optimality to excluding k-1 sets; checker.cpp tests every k-1 and k subset, validates exhaustive binomial trial counts, finds witnesses, and partitions all optima under exact generators. All counts and orbit distributions passed the actual standalone replay. A separate Python set-based implementation confirmed q<=6 and verified q=7 witness; a distinct linear integer formulation gave the same q=6 and q=7 optima. The proof is finite only; no extrapolation is claimed.

value.rationale: The sensor budget for location-identifying faults in a standard Kautz network is a natural graph-code invariant. The first failure of q-sensor placement occurs at q=6, continues at q=7, and has a large, exactly determined finite design census with a nontrivial reduction from 16 to 5 natural-symmetry types. Explicit feasible layouts and exact minimum counts are directly useful for short Kautz network design and tests of stronger code constraints, without claiming an asymptotic theorem.
